cells.tense: What you're growing is getting both your patience and your forward motion at once.
cells.act: perceive it with fresh eyes before judging
cells.ask: Sit with something you're growing as if meeting it the first time, before deciding anything about it — and decide after that, not during.
cells.core:
Tending something that's growing, you can be steady and quick at once. You say what you'll do, you do it, and the thing isn't trampled. On good days the people in it land somewhere calm — a call has been made, and they can see it holding. What feeds this is the slower half: looking at what's actually there before ruling on it. That half can go missing while the doing stays strong.

Sit with something you're growing as if meeting it for the first time. Before deciding anything about it. Then decide. You'll catch what you normally decide straight past. Because the caring is real, the call can wait several minutes and still come out clear. Nothing needs settling all at once — one honest look, then one call, and the look is what keeps the call about what's there rather than a version that isn't.
cells.sheetLine: Look at what's growing before you decide what to do with it.
cells.verb: charging first, setting boundaries by crossing them, cutting through inertia
cells.place: tending what needs to develop, creating conditions for growth

cells.tense: You are already several moves past the stage the thing is actually sitting in.
cells.act: reason it through fast and cleanly
cells.ask: Work something you're growing through on paper as it actually stands, cross out everything that's really about a later version, and act on what survives.
cells.core:
Tending something that's growing, you're charging out beyond the thing itself. You can see what it should become, and the plan is already three steps out; the small stage it's actually at gets hurried past. People pushed toward a self they haven't reached yet stop telling you where they truly are. You'd know that by looking, and you're busy thinking beyond it.

Work something you're growing through on paper as it actually stands, nothing idealized. Fast and clean. Then cross out everything that's really about a later version. Whatever survives is what moves it now. Notice what you ruled out — that's your judgment doing the caring, and it's a better thing to hand someone than a plan for who they haven't become yet. The plan can be right and still be early.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing for a flower while the thing is still a seed.

cells.tense: A call you were going to make hasn't happened yet, and you're still standing where you were.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Ask whoever knows this best what the single next step is, then take that one step sometime this week — nothing beyond it gets settled.
cells.core:
There's something you're tending that isn't getting your decisions. You stay near it — you know how it's going, you see what it needs, you watch — and the call it was waiting for hasn't come. Noticing isn't the gap. The gap is the moment a small yes or no was supposed to happen and quietly got left to next week, or to someone else, or to nobody. The thing is smaller for having waited, and you're still there beside it.

Ask whoever knows this best what the single next step is — not the whole plan. Then take that one step sometime this week. One inch. You don't need the full picture to move; the picture fills in behind you. A decision teaches you by being made, and nothing beyond it gets settled for now, so one inch is all you're agreeing to.
cells.sheetLine: You've been watching what needs care, and its decision hasn't come.

cells.tense: Something you're tending is taking its shape from your steady read on it, and you'd say you're only watching.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Notice, across a week, where your read is steering what you carry for someone — then set down what's finished and keep what's still needed.
cells.core:
You're likely steadier in a shared situation than you say you are. You talk little, and the shape of what happens still follows your hand. You carry people without naming it, and if asked you'd say you merely watch how things go. The people being carried don't need the account to match. Things run well around you, and whoever keeps them level doesn't have to be the one who says so.

Notice, across a week, where your read is steering what you carry for someone rather than just watching it. Then set down whatever's finished and keep what's still needed. The carry turns out smaller than the watching felt. What's growing gets a steadier hand once it's known it was being guided — and guiding is care you can name or simply keep doing, whichever fits.
cells.sheetLine: You're shaping what grows and calling it watching.

The reader could reasonably say 'I'm not standing behind a door — I just haven't needed to move yet,' so I'll narrow that to a plain present, not a motive. The ask survives if I'm wrong: any decision already made fits it. The sentence that serves me more than them would be the one that quietly hands them 'you are already a leader,' so I'll cut every version of it and say only what they'll do with a decision.
